source.title: Improving Autoregressive Visual Generation with Cluster-Oriented Token Prediction
source.authors: Teng Hu; Jiang-Ning Zhang; Ran Yi; Jieyu Weng; Yabiao Wang; Xian-Fang Zeng; Zhu-Cun Xue; Li-Zhuang Ma

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies autoregressive visual-generation training to image models and reports training-loss trends across parameter sizes, bearing on the claim’s extension to another modality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports visual-model training-loss curves and says losses decrease with model size, but it does not fit or assess a power-law form. Its FID, IS, precision, and recall results measure image-generation quality, not the loss or downstream measures named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper (IAR for autoregressive image generation). Its scaling evidence is qualitative. Training-loss curves are said to fall faster and lower with model size (B to XXL, 111M–1.4B), and FID/IS improve with size; the authors say this 'aligns with the scaling law'. There is no power-law fit, no held-out loss, no numeric loss values and no compute or token axis. The results cannot show whether the power-law form (V5) holds; they only show monotone improvement of the authors' own method with size. It invokes the scaling law to describe its method's performance rather than testing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that IAR (codebook rearrangement plus cluster-oriented cross-entropy) improves training efficiency and generation quality across 111M–1.4B models. They say it roughly halves training time for equal FID (42% in Sec. 4.2) and 'adheres to the scaling law'. That last statement rests on qualitative loss curves and FID trends, not on a fitted power law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses codebook rearrangement and a cluster-oriented cross-entropy objective for autoregressive visual generation, rather than measuring language-model held-out loss, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-loss curves are reported for different image-token resolutions and loss components; the paper also reports that generation metrics vary with classifier-free guidance and training setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-generation quality improves monotonically with parameter count for IAR on ImageNet 256 (FID 5.14, 3.18, 2.52, 2.19 for 111M to 1.4B; Table 1). Similar trends hold for LlamaGen and IAR in Table 2. No functional form is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generation-quality metrics (FID/IS) of autoregressive image models improve with parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-1 token and cluster prediction accuracy rises with model size for IAR and LlamaGen (e.g. IAR token top-1 2.62% to 3.88%, B to XXL; Table A6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Next-token prediction accuracy of AR image models increases with parameter count.

record.problems: The scaling-related loss evidence is training loss, not held-out loss; no power-law fitting or extrapolation is reported, and the loss curves are not given as numeric results in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-law loss rows were reported. Image-generation metric comparisons (FID, IS, precision, recall) and token-accuracy results were left out because they do not measure the loss or downstream outcomes specified in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form of loss in image AR models (no fit); held-out loss; data/compute scaling; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
No shape comparison at fixed parameters.

record.verdict_notes: Fig. 4(b) caption says '111M to 3B', but the text and tables cover only up to 1.4B. No row is labelled because the study does not test any version. The loss-curve rows are kept linked to V5 as cannot_determine for researcher visibility.

versions.untested_parts: Tests neither held-out language-model pretraining loss nor loss scaling in language models.
Does not fit on small runs and predict loss for larger runs.
Does not compare parameter/token allocations under fixed compute or fit compute-optimal trends.
Does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Reports image-model training-loss trends with parameter size, but does not fit or establish a power-law form, report held-out loss, or test other modalities and regimes such as video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not test downstream-task performance or its predictability from pretraining loss or scale.
Does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations across setups or fitting choices, or test curve bending.

rows.subject: IAR models (B, L, XL, XXL; aggregate trend reported)
rows.operation_detail: Reports training-loss curves across model sizes.
rows.value: The text says the loss decreases faster and converges to a lower value as model size increases; numeric values are not stated.
rows.note: Aggregate trend across model sizes; the reported trend does not establish a power-law form or held-out loss.
rows.check: Training loss, not held-out, read only from figure curves with no numbers. Four sizes with monotone decrease cannot show a power-law form. 'Partial' overstates what can be read.

rows.subject: IAR models (B, L, XL, XXL; aggregate trend reported)
rows.operation_detail: Reports training-loss curves across model sizes.
rows.value: The text says the loss decreases faster and converges to a lower value as model size increases; numeric values are not stated.
rows.note: Aggregate trend across model sizes; the paper notes that XL and XXL were trained on 16 × 16 tokens for 50 epochs. The reported trend does not establish a power-law form or held-out loss.
rows.check: Same as r1. Also confounded: per Table A1, XL/XXL on 16×16 tokens were trained for 50 epochs at a different LR (2e-4) while B/L ran 300 epochs, so the size comparison is not controlled.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
